readmeExcerpt:
# Uncodixify

GPT is surprisingly bad at UI design. If you ask it to generate interfaces long enough, you start noticing the same bad design-patterns repeating. Floating cards. Oversized rounded corners. Gradient-heavy dashboards. Decorative labels everywhere. Glass panels. After a while you can recognize a “GPT UI” immediately. This file exists to stop that. --- ## What this is `uncodixify.md` is a rule set that forces GPT to stop relying on its usual UI habits. Instead of letting it improvise design decisions, the file blocks the patterns it almost always falls back to and pushes it toward more normal interfaces. It doesn't try to teach GPT how to design. It mostly just tells it what **not** to do. ## Using it Include `uncodixify.md` in your prompt or system instructions when asking GPT to generate UI. Example:

Before (Typical GPT UI) | After (Uncodixified)

Before (Typical GPT UI) | After (Uncodixified) --- ## Agent Skill Uncodixfy is also available as an agent skill via `SKILL.md`. This works with AI coding agents that support the skill format, including Codex and Claude Code. #### All platforms. ``` npx skills add cyxzdev/Uncodixfy ``` Or bunx if you want. Once installed, invoke it with: ```text /uncodixfy ``` ## Star History

aiSummary.oneLiner: A strict Markdown rule set designed to prevent LLMs from generating repetitive and boilerplate UI code.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Uncodixfy provides a highly specific set of Markdown-formatted prompt rules that developers can prepend to their LLM queries when asking for UI code generation. It specifically targets the tendency of models to output overly verbose, identical, or poorly abstracted frontend components, particularly when using utility-first CSS like Tailwind. By laying out strict architectural guidelines—such as enforcing DRY principles and requiring distinct component abstractions—the rule set forces the LLM to write cleaner, more maintainable code on its first pass. It acts as a set of prompt engineering guardrails for frontend development.
keyFeatures: Markdown Rule Set: Easily copiable rules that can be pasted into any LLM conversation or system prompt.
Boilerplate Prevention: Explicitly instructs models to avoid repetitive patterns in their generated markup.
Component Abstraction: Forces the LLM to break down large UI structures into reusable sub-components.
Framework Agnostic: Designed to improve code generation quality across React, Vue, Svelte, or plain HTML.
Tailwind Optimization: Includes specific guidelines for preventing the generation of massive, unreadable utility class strings.
